items.ig_caption:
An unreleased AI model built five working exploit chains. 🤖

What Anthropic's Frontier Red Team described (via The Hacker News, 28 Oct):
→ An internal, unreleased model chained flaws into exploits for Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux, in lab tests
→ For Chrome it reported 62 flaws, all rated critical or high, including 13 sandbox escapes. Fixed in Chrome 156 (20 Oct)
→ The Linux proof of concept took 48 minutes to leak a kernel address and five more to reach a shell
→ All flaws went to vendors first; none were seen in real attacks
→ Anthropic doesn't say how much of each chain a human directed

Why it matters: the time from bug to working exploit is shrinking. Patch speed is now the control that matters most. Update browsers and kernels on a schedule you can measure.

cover.hook: Google's newest AI model goes to cyber defenders first.
cover.sub: Gemini 4 Carbon, announced 28 Oct, posts state-of-the-art scores at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities.

slides.title: Defenders first
slides.body: From this week, a subset of cyber defenders get access. Google will widen it to trusted partners through its Fairwind Program. There's no date yet for developers, businesses or consumers.

slides.label: SEC-bench Pro (finding vulnerabilities)
slides.note: ExploitGym 54.8% · CWE-bench patching 71.0% · evaluated without guardrails

slides.title: Fixing, not just finding
slides.body: Google says Carbon more than doubles Argon's success rate at generating secure code. Its Chrome team reported more than 10x better patch generation than another lab's large frontier model.

slides.title: Prompt injection: 0.0%
slides.body: Google reports 0.0% attack success on the Gray Swan indirect prompt injection benchmark, down from 0.7% for Argon. These are vendor numbers: test on your own workloads.

slides.title: What to do
items: Pick who on your team evaluates AI for bug triage
Review AI-written patches like any other code
Assume attackers get similar tools soon

items.x_text:
Magento / Adobe Commerce PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356, CVSS 9.3) is now in CISA KEV. Sansec says 953 stores carry a hidden loader in CMS blocks, about 471 via PolyShell, and it hides from scanners. Apply APSB26-73, audit cms_block.

#Magento #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
953 online stores. Hidden code that hides from security scanners. 🛒

What's been reported (The Hacker News, 26 and 28 Oct):
→ Sansec found a JavaScript loader injected into Magento CMS blocks on 953 stores, active since July 2025
→ About 471 were injected through PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356, CVSS 9.3), an unrestricted file upload flaw
→ The server checks whether the visitor is a shopper or a scanner, so scanners get nothing
→ The final payload is still unknown
→ CISA added PolyShell to its exploited-vulnerabilities list on 27 Oct

What to do: apply Adobe's APSB26-73 fix, check the cms_block and cms_page tables for blocks you didn't add, and audit admin accounts. One fully patched store was hit through a rogue admin.

cover.hook: Patched last week. Probed by attackers this week.
cover.sub: Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS 9.8): unauthenticated SQL injection that can chain to code execution.

slides.title: What the flaw does
slides.body: Horizon3.ai says an attacker who can reach the Thin Client Framework servlet can run SQL as the APPS database user, then OS commands as the EBS application account.

slides.label: CVSS · CVE-2026-101767
slides.note: Fixed in Oracle's October 2026 Critical Patch Update

slides.title: Probing has started
slides.body: Defused Cyber says its EBS decoys recorded "exploratory exploits" on 27 Oct. No successful exploitation is confirmed. An earlier EBS flaw, CVE-2025-61882, was used by the Cl0p extortion group.

slides.title: What's at stake
slides.body: Financial, payroll, HR and procurement records, plus internal systems an attacker can reach through the servlet.

slides.title: What to do
items: Can't yet? Drop /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer from the URL allowlist
Keep the EBS web tier on trusted networks

segments.say: Sixteen years. One bug that runs before Secure Boot.
segments.show: A UEFI firmware flaw in EDK II, from code committed in November 2010.
segments.card: 16 yrs|old flaw in EDK II firmware code

segments.say: Myth: Secure Boot protects every server. Reality: this flaw can run code before it, on network-booting servers.
segments.show: CVE-2026-97631, rated 9.5 by TianoCore. A 504-byte buffer overflow. Needs adjacent network access.

segments.say: No attacks seen yet, and most vendor fixes aren't out. If you don't need network boot, turn it off.
segments.show: Fix merged in EDK II on 15 Oct; no stable release yet. Project Mu builds 26 Oct. Watch AMI, Insyde, Phoenix.

items.x_text:
UEFI / EDK II CVE-2026-97631 (rated 9.5 by TianoCore): a 16-year-old buffer overflow can run code before Secure Boot on network-booting servers. Fix merged upstream, no stable release yet. No exploitation seen. Disable PXE if unused.

#Firmware #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
A 16-year-old firmware bug that can run before Secure Boot. 🧬

What The Hacker News reported (28 Oct):
→ CVE-2026-97631 in EDK II, the open-source UEFI code that AMI, Insyde, Phoenix and Microsoft's Project Mu build on
→ TianoCore rates it 9.5; the flawed code dates to a November 2010 commit
→ It's a 504-byte buffer overflow that hits network-booting servers; Red Hat and SUSE say it needs an adjacent network position
→ Found by Alex Matrosov (Anthropic) and Dan Holmes-Mitra (Google)
→ Fix merged upstream on 15 Oct, but no stable EDK II release yet. No exploitation seen

What to do: if you don't need PXE network boot, disable it, and watch for firmware updates from your server vendor.
